hint_ladder.title: Identify Function of Pronoun
hint_ladder.text: The blank is the subject of the verb 'agreed'. Subjects must be in the nominative case, not objective or possessive.

hint_ladder.title: Check Subject Position
hint_ladder.text: The pronoun performs the action 'agreed', so it must be in the nominative/subjective case. 'Them' is objective, 'their' is possessive, 'themselves' is reflexive.

hint_ladder.title: Select Subject Pronoun
hint_ladder.text: The subjective case for plural third person is 'they'. The committee members are plural, so 'they' is the correct subject pronoun.

hint_ladder.title: Final Choice
hint_ladder.text: Option A ('they') is the only subjective pronoun that fits as the subject of 'agreed'. The others are incorrect case forms.

C.text: 'Themselves' is a reflexive pronoun, used when the subject and object are the same (e.g., 'They hurt themselves'). There is no reflexive action here, so it is unnecessary.

D.text: 'Their' is a possessive pronoun, used to show ownership (e.g., 'their report'). It cannot serve as the subject of a verb. The subject must be 'they'.

next_time_rule: 💡 **Key Takeaway:** When a pronoun is the subject of a verb, use the nominative case: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Never use objective (me, him, them) or possessive (my, his, their) forms as subjects.
